correctness.rationale: Every two-independent family either lies in one pair-star or in a 4-ground-point edge set; intersections produce a 1-skeleton nerve, triangle 2-cells and octahedral S2 attaching spheres. Signed integral local cycle projected to relative triangle chains is the tetrahedral boundary; all 24 ground-point permutations have the expected orientation sign. Cohomotopy of a simply connected 2-skeleton, 3-skeleton cellular homology, Hurewicz and Whitehead give the all-n wedge type and integral exterior-power equivariance. Standalone independent face enumeration and mod-two and Lefschetz tests n=5..8 pass; no finite check is treated as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Explicit all-n simplex-three-skeleton classification and integral S_n top homology representation not implied by known n=5 Petersen instance, ordinary Kneser independence complexes, or higher-independence results for trees and other graph classes. Primary literature was read, and public mathematical-record queries were compared at the statement level. A residual unindexed-equivalence risk remains.
residual_risks: Indexed and public web literature searches do not exclude unindexed, newly posted or unpublished equivalent theorems.
Indexed public records for the special Petersen instance were compared as scientific statements; their entire external documentation was not needed to deduce the new general theorem.
The integral module depends on natural orientations of all attaching octahedra; the local 24-permutation sign check supports the global proof but is not an external independent verification.

value.rationale: Canonical and nonchordal infinite family; homotopy always concentrated in degree three despite graph and face dimensions increasing, with exact nontrivial binomial sphere multiplicity and integral S_n module. The octahedral attachment model explains structural stabilization; n>=6 cases genuinely move beyond the known isolated Petersen sphere and compare natural higher-independence topology with other Kneser constructions.
